paper.title: Algorithm 726: ORTHPOL - a package of routines for generating orthogonal polynomials and Gauss-type quadrature rules
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 20(1), 21-62 (March 1994), per the frame item and the shipped README
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/726.gz (article not fetched; ACM page not used)

code.commit: netlib CALGO archive 726.gz (shell archive with README, Makefile, r1mach.f, d1mach.f, test1.f to test8.f and the matching testN.out files)
code.archive: downloaded by scout 2026-11-27 from netlib.org/toms/726.gz (HTTP 200, 102785 bytes). sha256 of 726.gz: b229159f0bd9b38948f32ccb5f2d958c80f0a95c1706f88c03284aef5b0fa186 (scout download, 2026-11-27).
code.note: Gunzip the archive and unpack the shell archive with /bin/sh in an empty directory. Build test1.f with the shipped Makefile (it links r1mach.f and d1mach.f) and compare the output block with the shipped test1.out.

claim.location: Shipped reference output test1.out (inside 726.gz), first block, header 'output of test1 with modmom=.true.', row K=1, column DBETA(K). The block covers the weight ((1-om2*x**2)*(1-x**2))**(-1/2) on (-1,1) at om2=0.100, computed with modified moments (n=80).

reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.paper_value: DBETA(1) = 0.5065840806382684475158495727 at om2=0.1 as printed by the shipped test1 driver in double precision. The paper's Example 3.1 table is not read here; the README maps test1.f to Example 3.1.
claim.metric: DBETA(1) for om2 = 0.100 with modified moments (modmom=.true.), the double-precision value printed in test1.out, compared as an absolute number
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed weight, fixed om2, fixed n, no random numbers)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference is double precision (28 printed digits); the driver's own error column is about 1e-13 relative, so 1e-12 absolute allows compiler and libm differences in the Chebyshev-based modified-moment recurrence while still separating a wrong recurrence (typically errors far above 1e-10). Not to be loosened after any run. The modmom=.false. block (ordinary moments, ill-conditioned) is not claimed.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: one Fortran build of test1.f with its small helper routines and one run.
cost.data_licence: Netlib CALGO archive; licence per the archive's own notices (the rerun should record it).

why: The driver computes the recurrence coefficients of a weight with a singular endpoint behaviour from modified moments; the value DBETA(1) is not a closed form (beta_0 is an elliptic integral, but DBETA(1) needs the recurrence), so the rerun must execute the Fortran method.
